 “We couldn’t think of a better way to honor the milestone than by making ‘300’ a love letter to our dear friend and brother, Joe,” says showrunner Victor Teran.
 Samantha Highfill Wed, October 21, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Taylor Kinney as Kelly Severide and Joe Miñoso as Joe Cruz on 'Chicago Fire'
Credit: Peter Gordon/NBC Key Points
 Chicago Fire is preparing to say goodbye to one of its own.
 Entertainment Weekly has the exclusive first look at the drama's 300th episode.
 The hour will serve as a farewell for Joe Cruz (Joe Miñoso).
 Joe Cruz (Joe Miñoso) has been an important part of the Firehouse 51 family since the early days of Chicago Fire . Back in 2012, before One Chicago had expanded to include Chicago P.D. and Chicago Med , Chicago Fire won over viewers with its stories about a group of firefighters willing to do just about anything for one another ... aside from maybe clean the kitchen.
 Now in its 15th season, the show is still telling those stories. And when it comes to Miñoso, who appeared in season 1 before becoming a series regular in season 2, fans have watched his character, Cruz, handle a variety of situations, from inventing new, life-saving tools to losing dear friends to falling in love and starting a family.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement And of course, no matter what, he's always had Severide's ( Taylor Kinney ) back.
 Taylor Kinney as Kelly Severide on 'Chicago Fire' 
 Credit: Peter Gordon/NBC 
 As the show prepares for its milestone 300th episode, it also prepares to say goodbye to Cruz, who is currently in a wheelchair following an injury in the season premiere.
 Entertainment Weekly has the exclusive first look at the upcoming episode, which is simply titled, "Three Hundred." According to the logline, "Firehouse 51 responds to a complex hostage situation. Cruz continues to make strides while Chief Tomlin gives Severide an impossible task."
 Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter . 
 Taylor Kinney as Kelly Severide on 'Chicago Fire' 
 Credit: Peter Gordon/NBC 
 "We always knew that saying goodbye to a beloved character like Joe Cruz was going to be emotional. But change is part of life in any firehouse, so rather than shy away from that, we decided to lean into it and let those feelings drive a beautiful and complex story about family and friendship," showrunner Victor Teran tells Entertainment Weekly . "Joe Miñoso more than rose to the challenge and delivered a performance for the ages, which, by design, culminates in our 300th episode. Because we couldn't think of a better way to honor the milestone than by making '300' a love letter to our dear friend and brother, Joe."
 Advertisement Advertisement News of Miñoso's exit broke back in July , before the current season began airing. It shocked fans, though Fire viewers are familiar with the somewhat revolving door of the series.
 Miñoso is not the first major player to leave the show. He follows behind cast members Monica Raymund, Jesse Spencer, and Eamonn Walker, to name a few.
 The milestone 300th episode airs on Wednesday, Nov. 4 at 9 p.m. ET/PT on NBC.
